shadow_trades.reasoning_summary: Currently I have 1 each of A, B, C - a perfectly balanced bundle. Trading away my only A for another B would leave me with 0 A, 2 B, 1 C, which is less diversified and reduces utility given my preference for variety.

Currently I have equal quantities (1 each) of A, B, and C. This trade would make me have 2A, 0B, 1C, creating an imbalance and giving up my only B, which reduces variety. Since I value variety, this would decrease my utility rather than increase it.

Current bundle is balanced (1,1,1). Trading away my only B for 2 more A would leave me with 3A, 0B, 1C, which is heavily skewed and I'd lose variety entirely in B. Since I value variety, this reduces my utility.
Trading 1 C for 1 B would give me 2 B and 0 C, moving from an even 1-1-1 spread to an uneven bundle with a zero. Since I value variety, this reduces my utility rather than improving it.

Trading away my only B for another C would leave me with 1A, 0B, 2C, reducing variety and giving me two of the same good. Since I value variety, this trade would decrease my utility rather than increase it. I'd rather keep my even 1-1-1 distribution or trade for something that increases variety.

Current inventory is 1A/1B/1C, perfectly balanced. Trading away my only B for 2C would leave me with 1A/0B/3C, creating a worse imbalance (zero B, excess C). Since I value variety, this reduces my utility rather than increasing it.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my only A for another B would leave me with 0 A and 2 B, creating an imbalance and losing variety, which decreases my utility given my preference for balanced holdings.

Trading 1B for 1A would leave me with 2A, 0B, 1C — moving from an even 1-1-1 spread to an imbalanced one, which reduces variety value. Current equal distribution is already optimal for my variety-preference; this trade doesn't improve my utility.
Current inventory is balanced (1,1,1). Giving up my only B to get more A would create imbalance (3A,0B,1C), reducing variety value. Since I value variety, this trade decreases my utility.
Current inventory is balanced at 1 each. Trading away my only C for another B would leave me with 2 B and 0 C, reducing variety and utility. Rejecting to maintain balance.
Trading away my only B for another C would leave me with 0 B and 2 C, reducing variety and utility since I already have equal quantities of all three goods. This trade doesn't improve my bundle.

Trading away my only B (going from 1 to 0) to get C to 3 would create a lopsided bundle (1 A, 0 B, 3 C). Since I value variety, this reduces utility compared to keeping a more balanced inventory. I'd rather keep B and seek a trade that balances my holdings instead.
I currently have A:2, B:0, C:1. Trading 1 A for 1 B moves me to A:1, B:1, C:1, a perfectly balanced bundle, which maximizes value given my preference for variety.

Giving up 2 A for only 1 B would leave me with 0 A, 1 B, 1 C - trading a good I still need down to zero while over-paying. Better to negotiate a 1-for-1 trade instead to balance my inventory across A, B, C.

Currently I have A:2, B:0, C:1. Trading my only C for B would just swap which good is at 0, not improving variety - I'd go from (2,0,1) to (2,1,0), same imbalance. I'd rather keep C and get B from elsewhere without giving up my only C, or negotiate a trade that improves my worst-held good without eliminating another.

Currently I have A:1, B:0, C:2. Trading away my only A for a B would give me A:0, B:1, C:2 - still unbalanced but let's check value. Actually giving up my only A (which I have 1 of) for B (which I have 0 of) increases variety balance: before I have counts {1,0,2}, after {0,1,2} - same variance, no improvement. Reconsidering: this doesn't improve balance. Reject."

Currently I have A:1, B:0, C:2 - a very uneven bundle. Trading a C (which I have 2 of) for a B (which I have 0 of) moves me toward A:1, B:1, C:1, a perfectly balanced bundle that maximizes my variety-based utility.

Current inventory: A1,B0,C2. Trading away 2C for 1B would leave me A1,B1,C0 - losing all C and gaining B, which trades variety for zero of another good. Giving up 2C for only 1B is too steep since C would drop to 0. A better trade would be 1C for 1B to keep some C while gaining B.

Currently I have 2 A, 0 B, 1 C. Trading a surplus A (I have 2) for a B (I have 0) improves variety, moving me toward a more balanced 1-1-1 bundle, which increases my utility given diminishing value on repeated goods.

Giving up 2A for 1B would leave me with 0A, 1B, 1C - trading a scarce-ish good position for an imbalanced one. Currently I have A:2, B:0, C:1. Getting 1B for 1A would be fair (diversify), but giving 2A for 1B leaves me with only 1 total A and overpays. I'd rather negotiate a 1-for-1 trade instead.

Trading my only C (which I have 1 of) for B (which I have 0 of) would leave me with 2A, 1B, 0C - just shifting the scarcity from B to C without net improvement. I'd rather find a trade that adds variety without eliminating a good entirely, such as trading an A for B instead.

Current inventory is A:2, B:0, C:1, heavily imbalanced. Trading away 1 A (which I have plenty of) for 1 B (which I have none of) improves variety and balances my bundle to A:1, B:1, C:1 - ideal even distribution.

This trade would leave me with 0×A, 1×B, 1×C, going from a fairly diverse bundle to one with a zero holding, which hurts variety-driven utility. Giving up 2×A for only 1×B is too steep - I'd rather propose a 1-for-1 trade instead.

Trading away my only C would leave me with 0 C and 1 B, just shifting scarcity rather than improving variety. Current bundle A:2, B:0, C:1 would become A:2, B:1, C:0 - still uneven with two goods at extremes. I'd rather find a trade that gives me B without fully depleting C, or trade an A instead.
I have 2 A, 0 B, 1 C. Trading 1 A for 1 B moves me to 1 A, 1 B, 1 C - a perfectly balanced bundle, which maximizes utility given my preference for variety.

Giving up 2 A for 1 B would leave me with 0 A, 1 B, 1 C - trading two units for one is inefficient and would eliminate my A holdings entirely. I'd rather negotiate a 1-for-1 trade to balance my inventory across A, B, and C.

Currently I have A:2, B:0, C:1. Trading away my only C for B would just swap which good I have zero of, leaving me with A:2, B:1, C:0 - no real improvement in variety since I'd still have a good at zero. Better to seek a trade that gives me B without giving up my only C, or find one that improves overall balance more, e.g., trading A instead of C, since I have more A."}

Currently I have 2 A, 0 B, 1 C - a very unbalanced bundle. Trading 1 A (which I have excess of) for 1 B (which I have none of) moves me toward 1A/1B/1C, a more balanced and thus higher-utility bundle given my preference for variety.

This trade would leave me with 0 A, 1 B, 1 C - giving up all my A for just 1 B is too steep. Going from 2A/0B/1C to 0A/1B/1C trades a scarce good position for another scarce one but empties out A entirely, which hurts variety. I'd rather give up only 1 A for 1 B to balance my bundle to 1A/1B/1C, which would be ideal for variety-based utility."

Trading away my only C for B would leave me with 0 C and 1 B, just shifting the imbalance rather than improving variety. Currently I have 2 A, 0 B, 1 C - trading C for B gives 2 A, 1 B, 0 C, which is equally imbalanced. I'd prefer to keep C and acquire B without giving up my only C, or find a trade that improves diversity without creating a new zero-holding.

Trading away my only A would leave me with 0 A and 1 B, 2 C - still uneven, and I'd lose diversity in A entirely. Currently I have 1 A, 0 B, 2 C. Giving up A for B just swaps which good I'm missing, without improving overall balance. Better to seek a trade that adds B while keeping A, e.g. trading a C for a B.

I currently have 0 B and 2 C, so trading a surplus C for a scarce B improves variety and balances my inventory to 1 A, 1 B, 1 C - a perfectly even distribution which maximizes my utility given my preference for variety.

Giving up both my C for only 1 B would leave me with A:1, B:1, C:0 - trading away my only surplus good entirely and creating a new zero. Better to keep some C and only trade 1 for 1 B, preserving variety.
Trading away 1 A (of which I have 2) for 1 B (of which I have 0) improves variety balance across A, B, C, increasing my utility since I currently lack B entirely.

Giving up 2 A for 1 B would leave me with 0 A, 1 B, 1 C - trading my scarce-relative good excessively. Current: A=2, B=0, C=1. Losing both A's would overcorrect since I'd go from having variety in A to none, while only gaining 1 B. A better trade would be 1 A for 1 B to balance my bundle without depleting A entirely.

Currently I have 2 A, 0 B, 1 C. Trading away my only C for B would leave me with 2 A, 1 B, 0 C - just swapping which good I have zero of, not improving variety. I'd rather keep C and seek a trade that adds B without losing my only C, or trade an A instead.
